title: Hotspot-gradient allocator and micro-coalesce policy for KV cache fragmentation
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Problem summary: KV cache fragmentation on GPU reduces usable capacity for long-context models and increases OOMs during bursty continuous-batching workloads. Existing slab and slab-coalescer approaches cause scatter at allocation boundaries when token popularity shifts, and background compaction creates tail latency spikes.
tasks: Write compact design doc describing hotspot-gradient allocator (placement by access-gradient + age weight) and micro-coalesce policy (bounded background micro-writes per epoch)
Build offline simulator to model allocation/eviction under production token heatmaps and continuous-batching arrival patterns
Implement allocator core: gradient-weighted placement, epoch markers, soft-indirection mapping layer for in-place compaction
Add micro-coalesce worker that performs bounded, incremental coalesces aligned to CUDA streams to avoid blocking inference
Integrate placement hints from popularity predictor (sampling from request traces) and expose tuning knobs via runtime config
Add telemetry: fragmentation_ratio, avg_free_run, micro_coalesce_work_per_sec, coalesce_latency_p95, kv_eviction_rate
Benchmark on dedicated GPU nodes with synthetic and replayed traffic; iterate parameters to meet latency and throughput SLOs
Create safety rollouts: feature flag, canary in staging, 5% prod, 25% prod, full ramp; implement abort and automatic rollback triggers
Write integration + e2e tests, plus chaos test to validate safety during preemption and OOM events
Produce PR and run perf review + security review if needed
acceptance_criteria: Lab simulator shows >=50% reduction in fragmentation_ratio (free memory scatter index) compared to current slab baseline for mixed hot/cold workloads
Micro-coalesce worker maintains background CPU/GPU overhead <5% of inference cycle and p95 coalesce latency <50ms under typical load
End-to-end tests show no regression beyond 3% throughput drop and tail latency increase <=5ms at 95th/99th percentiles
Staging canary (5%) runs for 72h without OOM incidents or user-visible errors
Telemetry dashboards show stable coalesce work and no spike-correlated errors; rollout has documented abort conditions
notes: Design rationale: combine access-gradient (short-term popularity slope) with age-bias to prefer packing newer hot tokens into contiguous micro-slabs, leaving older cold allocations in dedicated cold pools to minimize fragmentation
Micro-coalesce policy purpose: limit per-epoch compaction work to small, deterministic chunks to avoid latency cliffs; use prioritized queue ordering by expected reduction-in-fragmentation-per-byte

Indirection layer: small logical-to-physical pointer table to allow in-place compaction with pointer swaps instead of large memmoves; table size tuned to occupancy and must be GPU-resident for lookup speed
GPU memory layout considerations: align micro-slabs to warp-friendly boundaries (e.g., 128B) to keep kernel access coalesced; place hot micro-slabs on high-bandwidth memory banks where possible

Continuous batching interactions: batching increases allocation churn; we sample batched request traces to build arrival-rate-aware placement heuristics; try to align batch-adjacent prefixes to contiguous slots to leverage KV cache prefix hits
Trade-offs considered: increased metadata overhead (indirection table) vs. reduction in fragmentation; overhead acceptable if fragmentation reduction >30% and OOMs drop significantly
Fallback strategy: if compaction pressure causes latency regressions, fall back to conservative best-fit allocator and disable micro-coalesce until resolved
comments: 2025-03-12 Priya Natarajan: Kickoff. Drafted initial design and simulator plan. Assigned Miguel as owner. Shared initial sketches in #kv-alloc channel.

2025-03-14 Miguel Santos: Implemented baseline simulator and ingestion of two weeks of anonymized request traces from prod-replay. Early runs show fragmentation_ratio ~0.32 baseline; prototype gradient placement reduces to ~0.18 in one scenario.

2025-03-16 Performance Review: Carlos (Perf Eng) reviewed approach — liked indirection idea but asked for quantifying pointer-table lookup overhead. Suggested GPU L2 locality tests and microbench harness.
2025-03-17 Design Feedback: Anika (Infra PM) requested rollout abort conditions to be explicit: 3 OOMs within 1h or >10% increase in p99 latency. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-18 Miguel Santos: Implemented micro-coalesce worker prototype using CUDA streams; initial microbench shows coalesce latency p95 ~42ms with work cap tuned to 512KB/epoch. CPU overhead ~2.1% on driver node.
2025-03-19 Miguel Santos: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1542 with allocator + simulator tests. Triggered CI perf suite.
2025-03-20 QA: Staging run scheduled for next week. Added additional telemetry (coalesce_efficiency = bytes_coalesced / work_bytes) and a dashboard template.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for staging cluster and run perf/regression suite (24h).
Prod canary 1: 5% traffic for 72h. Monitor fragmentation_ratio and OOMs. Abort if abort conditions hit.
Prod canary 2: 25% traffic for 72h. Expand if stable.
Ramp to 100% with gradual scale in 2-day increments while monitoring telemetry
risks: Indirection table increases lookup overhead; could regress single-request latency if not GPU-resident or poorly cached
Compaction work could compete with inference kernels for memory bandwidth if not scheduled carefully
Edge cases under preemption (spot GPU reclaim) may leave indirection inconsistent; need robust recovery logic
Telemetry blind spots: need to ensure fragmentation metric is accurate and debounced to avoid false aborts
